general_information.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_information.Description: Objectives: After completing the course, students will understand the background, operations, and structure of travel agency and tour operation. Students will understand the differences between tour operator and travel agency, and will be able to examine and evaluate how these two types of businesses operate as a foundation for future professional growth. Description: This subject covers Travel Agency philosophy, ideas, and prerequisites for running a travel agency firm. Practical case studies from travel agencies worldwide and in Vietnam will be interspersed with these principles. In these case studies, students must discuss and work in groups so that teachers can assess their knowledge and expertise through presentations and tests.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend at least 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination - Actively participate in class activities - Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class - Use their own laptop in class only for learning purposes - Read the textbook in advance - Access the course website (http://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online support from teachers and other students, and for practicing and assessment.

description: Objectives: After completing the course, students will understand the background, operations, and structure of travel agency and tour operation. Students will understand the differences between tour operator and travel agency, and will be able to examine and evaluate how these two types of businesses operate as a foundation for future professional growth. Description: This subject covers Travel Agency philosophy, ideas, and prerequisites for running a travel agency firm. Practical case studies from travel agencies worldwide and in Vietnam will be interspersed with these principles. In these case studies, students must discuss and work in groups so that teachers can assess their knowledge and expertise through presentations and tests.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Understand the basic operations, organizational structure, historical evolution, main characteristics and quality standards of a travel agency"
Describe the primary functions of a travel agency and clarify how these functions seamlessly integrate with the operations of other service businesses throughout a tour.
Examine the similarities and contrasts between a travel agency and a tour operation to better understand the distinctions between these two types.
Maintain ethical and professional conduct standards is of the utmost importance in the tourism industry
Determine the structure of the travel agency, and list of businesses along with their respective functions in the tourism industry is provided.
Identify the environmental repercussions, the social, cultural and economic effects that travel agencies have on the countries that they serve as destinations.
Desmontrate good skills, tactics, and attitudes to carry out the basic duties of a travel agency executive.
Discuss the relationship between the transportation industry, tour operators, and travel agencies.
Apply learned knowledge to analyze travel agency strategies through case studies

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: All knowledge which belong to every single block.
assessments.Grading Guide: Students will work in groups of 4-5 students and will be assigned to be in charge of a case study stated in the syllabus (assigned by the instructor) related to the topics in each block learned in the lessons. last week. They must analyze the case study by answering the questions raised in the case.

Participation grade will be given based on students' preparation, and quantity as well as quality of participation in classroom; quality of participation is demonstrated through asking relevant questions, making statements that add to and facilitate class discussion, and builds upon others’ comments. Class preparation and pre-reading before lecture will be assessed upon individuals' understanding and ability to answer questions in the class. Individuals will be called up randomly to be assessed.

assessments.No Question: Written report: limitation of 4000 words Presentation: 30 mins/group
assessments.Grading Guide: Each group prepares and presents to the class a plan/idea for operating/business development for their travel agency: Objective: what needs to be achieved (in-depth analysis) Requirements in the plan: clearly present elements that cover the necessary characteristics of a travel agency mentioned in the learning blocks, travel companies/agencies depending on the student's ideas. It can be a start-up or a company with many years of experience in the industry. Students need to note that each different nature of tourism business will have different requirements and knowledge. Students must submit reports in both written and oral form
